newsitem.title: UK: BAe retreats on profit-taking after results.
newsitem.headline: BAe retreats on profit-taking after results.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace Plc retreated on profit-taking after an initial run-up immediately after the group released its annual results.
By 1113 GMT, the shares were off 18-1/2p at 1254, having risen as high as 1295 earlier.
BAe posted annual pre-tax profit of 456 million stg, at the top end of the range of analysts' forecasts.
The shares had jumped by 82-1/2p, or 6.9 percent, from February 12 to Tuesday.
Panmure Gordon analyst Paul Pickford said he recommended clients take profits this morning on the back of the recent rally.
"It was an excellent set of figures and things look good going forward," Pickford said.
However, he added, "the key to further outperformance is consolidation in Europe and it could be 12 months before we hear anything on that. I think that's being reflected in the (lower) share price."
Zafar Khan, an analyst with SocGen, said the decline in the share price may have been linked to expectations that the aerospace group's Tornado deliveries to Saudi Arabia will peak this year.
But Khan said he raised his 1997 and 1998 profit forecasts to 545 million from 515 million and to 615 million from 595 million, respectively.
Khan, who maintained a "buy" rating on the stock, said he had upgraded his estimates based on better-than-expected defence and interest income.
SBC Warburg, meanwhile, said it reiterated its "buy" recommendation this morning after the company released its earnings.
